text:
None of these four establishes the exact combination of short-/long-term pooled embeddings, a learned fusion gate, and an added SASRec residual. [SHAN](https://opus.lib.uts.edu.au/bitstream/10453/126040/1/ijcai2018_Yin.pdf) attention-pools historical items, then attends jointly over that representation and recent-session items. Its SHAN-L/SHAN-S ablations test long-only/recent-only; fusion usually helps, but recent-only wins Tmall Recall@20. [HGN](https://arxiv.org/html/1906.09217) instead combines a persistent user embedding, feature-/instance-gated recent-item pooling, and a separate history-to-candidate item-product term. Its ablations isolate gates, pooling, and that direct similarity term—not adaptive versus fixed temporal fusion.

[FOSSIL](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/icdm16a.pdf) combines a normalized historical embedding sum with weighted recent-item Markov components. Its learned user/lag weights provide personalized additive fusion, rather than a context-dependent neural gate; it is a particularly relevant similarity-shortcut control. [LSIDN](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.14743v1) is the closest adaptive-fusion precedent: session encoders and pooling, recurrent interest evolution, and a target-conditioned sigmoid gate mixing long-/short-term representations. It tests removing either interest branch and either denoising strategy, but does not report a fixed-versus-adaptive fusion ablation. It explicitly addresses unintentional and inter-session noise through contrastive learning and session separation. SHAN/HGN learn interaction importance, but this does not establish explicit suppression of isolated interactions; FOSSIL has no dedicated denoising mechanism.

Recommended controls, inferred from these distinctions: identical SASRec backbone plus recent-only pooling, long-only pooling, fixed fusion, and adaptive fusion; also SASRec alone and SASRec plus an ungated pooled-history candidate-dot-product term. Hold embeddings, scoring, training, and validation protocol constant. Add isolated-interaction perturbation/removal checks before claiming denoising: improved ranking alone cannot distinguish temporal adaptation from an additive similarity shortcut.
